summary:
Implemented the Tabs widget per the spec, without running anything or committing.

Changed/added files:
- src/textual/widgets/tabs.py (new): Tab, TabsRenderable, Tabs (exports Tab and Tabs via __all__; can_focus = True; DEFAULT_STYLES "height: 2;"; private reactives _active_tab_name and _bar_position; watch__active_tab_name animates the bar; on_key, activate_* methods, find_tab_by_name, action_range_clicked).
- src/textual/renderables/underline_bar.py: yields one Text object; new clickable_ranges parameter before width; click spans attached last in mapping order; early path adds no click metadata.
- src/textual/renderables/opacity.py: blended color merged into existing style, preserving attributes and click metadata.
- docs/reference/tabs.md (new): single ::: directive for textual.widgets.tabs.Tabs.
- tests/renderables/test_underline_bar.py: three new tests appended; existing tests unchanged.
- tests/test_tabs.py (new): naming, equality, duplicates, lookup, activation, wrap-around, first-character search, click metadata and dimming, no-tabs and auto-fit row layout.

Not done / unverified:
- Nothing was executed, so all tests are unverified.
- The layout resolver needed no change: Edge already has size, min_size, and fraction with the specified defaults.
- The optional sandbox demo was skipped.
- Known issue: with duplicate names, the bar position (a full-list index from find_tab_by_name) can be misaligned with the displayed tabs, so the highlight may land on the wrong tab. The spec's wording forces this; the index is wrapped modulo the displayed count so nothing raises.
- A zero-width label gets a one-cell share because the resolver treats size 0 as flexible.
- Nothing was committed.
